rows.description: A preschooler says ouch when hurt, oops after a mistake and wow at something wonderful. The words tell how they feel in the moment, and a gentle reply, such as it is okay, teaches recovery from small errors.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: curiosity, awe, hurt

rows.description: A child learns that shh means be quiet or be careful and ooh shows interest or delight. Tone decides the meaning, since a soft shh comforts and a sharp shh can scold; a child reads the voice before the sound.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child practises a quiet voice in a library and a loud voice on the playground. Learning volume control takes time, and reminders with a visual cue work better than shouting to be quiet.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler whispers to share a secret, to hide or to be quiet. Whispers can show closeness or mischief; a child taught that secrets from trusted adults about touch or harm are not okay should tell a grown-up.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young child whose voice cracks or quavers when speaking before a class may be nervous or about to cry. Naming it kindly, such as saying it is normal to feel wobbly, helps more than telling the child to stop.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler hears a soft voice as safe and a harsh voice as anger or danger, even when the words are neutral. Children need help learning that a loud harsh voice is not always about them.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child who speaks in a hesitant, halting way may be shy, searching for a word, or unsure of a response. Waiting calmly works better than finishing sentences for the child.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler with big news may speak in a rushed tumble of words and skip parts. A patient adult who says slow down, I want to hear it all helps the child organize the story.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child whose sentence trails off may have lost the words, feel unsure they are allowed to say them, or be afraid of a reaction. Gentle prompting such as what happened next helps without pressure.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler learns that conversation involves waiting; silence after a question may mean thinking, shyness or not understanding. A wise adult counts to five before rephrasing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
